messages:
marie: quick sync — I ran a cross-model perf sweep this morning, comparing kernel stacks + batching heuristics across Llama-70B, Mistral-7B v0.2, Mixtral-8x7B, and Qwen-7B. Posting raw takeaways and a few config recs.

aj: thanks — super useful. did you include long-context (32k) runs?

marie: yes. test matrix: context lengths = [512, 4k, 32k], batch sizes = [1,4,8,16], kernels = [flash_attn, cuDNN_fused, cuda_fallback], kv strategies = [per_gpu_shard, shared_ram_cache]. latency = p50/p95, throughput = tokens/sec.

perf-bot: profiling summary links: flamegraphs + kernel timelines -> https://perf.internal/redwood/1752004321 ; cpu/gpu overlap charts attached in the doc.

deniz: top-level notes?

marie: TL;DR: Mistral-7B best latency/throughput at small batch sizes with flash_attn. Llama-70B strongly benefits from cuda_fallback for very long contexts (32k) due to kv cache memory layout; flash_attn blows memory and thrashes. Qwen-7B regressed ~12% on p95 for 4k->32k after latest cuDNN update — looks like a kernel selection change. Mixtral sits in the middle but is very batch-friendly up to batch=8.

samir: can you paste numbers for Llama-70B 32k? trying to reason about kernel fallback tradeoffs.

marie: Llama-70B 32k, batch=1:
```
flash_attn: OOM on A100-40GB (kv thrash)
cuda_fallback: p50 420ms, p95 720ms, tokens/sec 1900
cuDNN_fused: p50 480ms, p95 830ms, tokens/sec 1700
```
Batch=4 (cuda_fallback wins for throughput): p50 380ms, tokens/sec 6800.

leo: interesting — memory layout for kv seems to be the culprit. did you profile KV write/stall times?

marie: yes — KV write stalls dominate on flash_attn for long contexts; write spikes at every layer when sequence > 8k. We see >40% GPU idle waiting on memcpy in that stack. With cuda_fallback we get a more compact KV packing that reduces memcpy spikes.

aj: what about batching heuristics? any rule-of-thumb per model?

marie: my recommended heuristics:
```
- Mistral-7B: prefer flash_attn, target_batch_sizes = [1,4], max_batch_tokens ~= 12k
- Mixtral-8x7B: prefer cuDNN_fused at batch<=8, use continuous small batches for real-time (preferred burst path)
- Llama-70B: default to cuda_fallback for context > 8k; allow flash_attn for <=4k if memory headroom
- Qwen-7B: pin to previous cuDNN kernel (v8.x) until we validate new kernel for kv layout
- KV: per_gpu_shard for dedicated pools; shared_ram_cache better for small models on multi-tenant hosts
```
These are conservative — we can be more aggressive if we add KV prefetching.

deniz: perf-regression note on Qwen — can you share diff of kernel selection before/after the cuDNN auto-picker change?

marie: yes — the auto-picker started choosing cuDNN_fused for attention forward/back on mid-length sequences, which increases intermediate buffer sizes and pushes kv memcpy into slow paths. Reverting to pinned cuDNN v8.2 + a manual kernel override returned p95 to baseline.

samir: any observable quality tradeoffs with the cuda_fallback path (quantization / precision)?

marie: no measurable generation quality change in our eval prompts. We measured token-level logprobs and embedding cosine similarity (0.998 vs baseline). Quantized kernels behave same as long as we keep fp16 accumulation for some layers.

leo: what about batch limits? e.g., Mixtral at what batch size does latency tail blow up?

marie: Mixtral-8x7B: latency p95 starts rising after batch=8 when context ~4k. At batch=16 we see p95 +40%, tokens/sec only +10% vs batch=8 — diminishing returns. Recommendation: cap user-facing interactive batch to 8, allow queued offline to 16+.

aj: KV cache eviction behavior — anything surprising?

marie: yes — when we use shared_ram_cache on hosts with noisy neighbor IO, eviction churn increased and our prefix cache hit rate dropped ~18% on Llama workloads. For Dedicated pools per_gpu_shard avoids this but costs more memory. So we should prefer per_gpu_shard for enterprise/Dedicated.

deniz: do we need runtime switches in the serving config? e.g., model.profile -> kernel_override, batching_preset?

marie: proposed runtime flags (P0):
```
model.profile: "small_interactive" | "large_context" | "batch_throughput"
kernel_override: "flash_attn" | "cuda_fallback" | "cuDNN_fused"
batching_preset: "interactive" | "throughput"
kv_strategy: "per_gpu_shard" | "shared_ram_cache"
```
These allow quick fallbacks without redeploying.

samir: noted. who will own the rollout plan to pin Qwen kernels?

marie: I'll own immediate rollback and we should add a canary with metrics: p95 latency, tokens/sec, kv-mmcpy-time. @aj can you add the test to the nightly regression suite?

aj: yes, will add Qwen 4k/32k kernel matrix to nightly and a gating alert if p95 regresses >5% vs baseline.

leo: one more ask — can we add a small synthetic workload that stresses KV writes to CI? current CI misses those stalls.

marie: will add a microbench that simulates 32k prefixes + 1 token generation per step, across 8 layers. Perf-bot will collect kernels and nvprof traces.

perf-bot: created ticket PERF-3221 for Qwen kernel pin + CI microbench.

marie: ok team, thanks — I'll push a short runbook for runtime flags and we can discuss longer-term: KV prefetch + compact kv layout in the runtime.

aj: thanks marie :thumbsup:
